text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

AMP Society chief executive officer George Turnbull yesterday announced the board's decision to demutualise the country's largest financial institutional, with two million Australians set to share in a A$10 billion handout. The move involves a name change and will see AMP form a new holding company which will control subsidiaries that operate Australian, New Zealand and UK life insurance businesses, the Priority One mortgage arm, general insurance and investment activities. Page 1.

After less than a year after being appointed to manage BHP Co Ltd's long-awaited fourth business arm, former Magma Copper chief executive J. Burgess Winter announced his departure yesterday. BHP said Winter had left "to pursue a range of business and personal interests". Page 1.

Steel unions have called off a national strike planned for today, after BHP Steel offered a new wage agreement which would deliver pay rises and bonuses worth up to 15 per cent over the next two years. Union delegates will meet to consider the company's latest pay offer next week, but sources say workers would not be required to trade off any of their existing entitlements or conditions in return for the pay rises. Page 3.

ICI Australia is looking for partners to help bear the cost of a A$2 billion world-scale petrochemical plant in Western Australia that would be fed by natural gas from the North-West Shelf. Other chemicals groups, such as Dow Chemicals and Formosa Plastics, have also looked at securing gas supplies from the North-West Shelf, meaning the companies may have to fight a battle for the rights to buy the ethane gas needed to feed such a plant. Page 25.

As part of a wholesale shake-up of the board and senior management of TNT Ltd to clear the way for KPN's A$2 billion takeover, chairman Fred Millar has stepped down. Managing director David Mortimer also quit at the board meeting held in London on Wednesday, but will remain as the chief executive and chairman of the combined time-sensitive freight and logistics venture in Australia, Asia and the Americas. Page 25.

With the Australian Securities Commission yet to identify Mark Booth, TNT Ltd's mystery trader who made A$2 million profit from purchasing call options, it will today ask the Federal Court to distribute the profit to the options holders from whom Booth mae the purchase. Page 25.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Investment giant, the AMP Society, revealed its aggressive multi-billion dollar expansion plans after announcing its plans to demutualise and list on the stock market. AMP chief executive George Turnbull said the Society had A$5 billion to invest and it was focusing on a substantial acquisition in the United States and the United Kingdom. Page 21.

Construction group Leighton Holdings Ltd has snapped up Telstra subsidiary Visionstream for an estimated A$25 million. Visionstream is responsible for building and managing Telstra's A$4 billion pay TV network, with the ongoing contract to build the remainder of the Telstra cable rollout which is to pass a further two million Australian households. Page 21.

BHP Copper founding chief executive Burgess Winter has resigned just 12 months after the group's A$3.2 billion acquisition of US-based Magma Copper Co. Winter is retiring to pursue "business and personal interests" and will be succeeded on January 1 by Ji Lewis, BHP's executive general manager of corporate development. Page 21.

After a two-year legal battle, Qantas Airways Ltd yesterday began negotiations with new airline hopeful Aussie Airlines Ltd. The talks may result in the start-up airline securing terminal space at five Australian airports. However, the terms of the negotiations and Aussie's threat of a damages claim against Qantas are still unclear. Page 21.

Canadian media group, CanWest Global Communications, is believed to have agreed to inject A$137 million into the purchase of a further 20 per cent of Ten Group Ltd, operator of the Ten television network. The move would lift CanWest's interest in Ten to 76 per cent as it prepares the network for a planned stock exchange listing. Page 21.

The Chairman of the Federal Government inquiry into financial services, Stan Wallis, has appeared to back away from recommendations to reform the tax system. Even though a wide range of taxation issues were raised in submissions into the inquiry, Wallis conceded that his ambitions to cover such reforms would have to be shelved as the terms of reference for the inquiry excluded matters concerning taxation. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The AMP Society has signalled that it could spend up to A$5 billion on worldwide acquisitions to consolidate its position as a major life company. Managing director George Turnbull said the group had a number of possible acquisitions in focus, but he also ruled out any AMP plans of buying a bank or reinsurance company. Page 21.

The Australian Securities Commission will apply to the Federal Court today to seize the A$2 million profit made by the mysterious Mark Booth from trading in TNT stock to compensate the investors from whom he bought them. The ASC has not yet found Booth after it launched an investigation into alleged insider trading of TNT shares two months ago. Page 23.

Canadian proprietor, Izzy Asper, has spent A$136 million as his media group, Can West Global Communications, purchased a further 10 per cent of Ten Group - the owner of the Ten television network. It is believed the Federal Government will remind Asper that the transaction is not within the spirit of the law governing foreign ownership of TV networks. Page 23.

According to a new survey conducted by AIS Media Futures, it has been revealed that advertisers were predicting a 7.5 per cent increase in advertising budgets for next year. However, media executives held a much gloomier picture tipping a rise of just 3.6 percent. Page 23.

Qantas Airways has settled a dispute with the Federal Airports Corporation, which will see it negotiate with Aussie Airlines operator Brian Grey over the sub-leasing of domestic terminal gates and withdraw an application for a Federal Court injunction against the FAC, after the FAC agreed to withdraw breach-of-lease notices issued last month. Page 23. --

Anaconda Nickel's A$900 million Murrin Murrin project could face delays of at least several months, with the Murrin Murrin Foundation, set up by Anaconda to resolve a string of native title claims, on the verge of collapse and the company set to battle an environmental appeal by the Environmental Protection Authority. Page 25.
THE AGE

The president and chief executive of BHP's recently formed global copper division, Burgess Winter, has decided to retire 18 months ahead of expectations. The 63-year-old is the former president and chief executive officer of Magma Copper and was BHP's exception to its rule of retiring senior executives at 62. Page C1.

Announcing the AMP Society's proposed sharemarket listing yesterday, managing director George Turnbull said the group was looking at spending up to A$5 billion on acquisitions. However, Turnbull ruled out buying a bank, dampening speculation that AMP would seek to become a key player in the banking sector after the Federal Government considers the Wallis inquiry report in March. Page C1.

Normandy Mining chief Robert Champion de Crespigny said yesterday he was amazed that Societe Generale and other institutions had refused to accept Normandy's takeover bid for Northern Territory gold miner North Flinders. Labelled a mistake by Crespigny, he said rejection of the offer frustrates plans by Normandy to move to full ownership of Flinders. Page C3.

As Dutch postal and telecommunications group KPN moves to complete its takeover of TNT, a number of changes have taken place in the boardroom. At a board meeting in London yesterday, TNT announced that chairman Fred Millar had resigned, being replaced by KPN executive Ad Scheepbouwer. David Mortimer will stay on as a director of TNT and Andre Chen and John Yates have been appointed joint managing directors of TNT. Page C3.

According to the 1997 AIS Media Futures Study, national advertisers are predicting a 7.5 per cent increase in advertising expenditure next year, while media companies are forecasting lower growth, at just 3.6 per cent for the year. The survey also found that most of the advertisers planned to spend their money on television advertising. Page C3.

CanWest Global Communications has agreed to spend A$136 million to buy a further 10 per cent of the Ten Group from Jack Cowin and Robert Whyte. If the move is approved by various authorities, CanWest's economic interest in Ten will increase from 66 per cent to 76 per cent, but its voting interest will stay at 15 per cent. Page C3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
